text:
charlie_customer: Hey team — our app started getting 502s to the Redwood API after we cut over a proxy yesterday. Repro steps below, can you help?

alice_support: @charlie_customer sorry to hear that. Can you paste the curl output and a DNS resolution for the hostname?

charlie_customer: Sure. From one of our app hosts: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.com
10.0.30.45

$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
* Connected to 10.0.30.45 port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS 1.2 connection to 10.0.30.45:443
* error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:wrong version number
* Closing connection 0
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS alert, Client hello (1):
curl: (35) error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:wrong version number
```

alice_support: Thanks. That IP (10.0.30.45) is one of your internal proxy IPs, not an AWS interface endpoint. Do you have a Private Hosted Zone or custom Route53 record for api.redwood-inference.com?

charlie_customer: We do have a PHZ for redwood-inference.com — we added an A record to point api.* to our internal proxy (for internal telemetry). I thought the interface endpoint would take precedence.

bob_netops: Route53 PHZs are authoritative inside the VPC. If you created a private hosted zone for redwood-inference.com and associated it with the VPC, it will override the interface endpoint private DNS. That explains why your app is hitting the proxy IP.

alice_support: Yep — that's a split-horizon conflict. The interface endpoint relies on the AWS-created private DNS record for api.redwood-inference.com which resolves to the endpoint ENI. If you have a PHZ with the same zone and a matching A record, the PHZ wins.

charlie_customer: So what's the recommended fix? We need internal telemetry to go to our proxy, but traffic to Redwood API needs to go to the PrivateLink endpoint.

dave_oncall: Options: (1) delete/modify the PHZ record for api.redwood-inference.com and let the endpoint DNS resolve to ENI IPs; (2) keep PHZ but change the record to point to the VPCE ENI IPs (fragile); (3) move proxy traffic to a subdomain (telemetry.internal.example) so it doesn't collide.

charlie_customer: We tried option 2 earlier — added the endpoint ENI IPs as A records in the PHZ, but the ENI IPs changed after a restart and broke again.

alice_support: Right — VPCE ENI IPs are not stable long-term. We don't recommend managing them as static records. Best path: remove the PHZ record for api.redwood-inference.com and either: 1) use Route53 resolver rules to forward only telemetry.* to your proxy, or 2) move telemetry to a different domain/subdomain.

charlie_customer: Ok will do. Quick question — is there any risk of traffic leaking to the public internet while we change this?

bob_netops: If PHZ points to your proxy that's inside the VPC, traffic stays internal. If you delete the PHZ record and the VPCE private DNS is enabled, resolution will point at the VPCE ENIs and traffic will stay on AWS private network. The leak risk is when DNS resolves to a public IP (no PHZ and no VPCE private DNS).

alice_support: To be safe, take these steps: 
1) Verify the VPCE private DNS setting is enabled in the console for the interface endpoint.
2) Confirm there is no public A record for the hostname. 
3) Apply the PHZ change during a maintenance window and test from a non-prod host first: 
```
# test before change
dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @172.31.0.2   # VPC DNS resolver
# after removing PHZ record:
dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @172.31.0.2
# should return multiple ENI IPs like 10.0.x.x
```

infra-bot: [automated] VPCE api.redwood-inference.com: private-dns=ENABLED, service=vpce-svc-0abc123def, state=available

charlie_customer: We removed the A record for api.redwood-inference.com from our PHZ and now `dig` shows the endpoint ENIs. Curl to /v1/health returns 200. Everything looks healthy. 

alice_support: Great! Thanks for confirming. For follow-up, consider: 
- Move telemetry to telemetry.redwood-inference-internal (or similar).
- Use Route53 Resolver rules to forward only the telemetry subdomain to your proxy.
- Avoid hardcoding VPCE ENI IPs in DNS.

charlie_customer: Thanks all for the quick help :thumbsup: — closing the ticket on our side.

alice_support: Glad it worked — ping us if anything else pops up.
